chapter_title: Concerning the Five Saviours, the Resurrectors of Those Who Are Dead, Together with the Five Resurrections
chapter_note: This kephalaion is structurally pentadic (enumerating resurrectors) with a clear hagiographic opening frame and a likely late concluding beatitude. The central numbered sequence (¶3–¶6) is impersonal, cosmological, and process-oriented, consistent with the older teaching substrate, though heavily lacunose.

paragraphs.temporal_note: Formulaic dialogue/frame opener (“Once again the enlightener speaks”), characteristic of the compiled Kephalaia hagiographic apparatus.
Too fragmentary to date internally, but it appears to continue the broken opening frame line begun in ¶1 rather than the pentadic teaching proper.
Bare enumerative item within a pentadic teaching list; no address, no citation, no institutional application—fits the impersonal schematic substrate despite the lacuna.

paragraphs.core_text: And the third resurrector is the Father, the First [...], because by his word shall all lives [...] gather in and go to him, and they receive [...] and rest.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Cosmic mechanism stated as process (“by his word… gather… receive… rest”), remaining within the cosmological system (no contemporary institutions or exhortation).

paragraphs.core_text: The fourth resurrector is the Light Mind, because [...]. ⟨p.46⟩
paragraphs.temporal_note: Another pentadic list item naming a cosmological entity (Light Mind) in the same schematic style; manuscript page marker preserved.

paragraphs.core_text: The fifth resurrector to the good [...] is the Father, the First established one [...]. [He ...] all the powers, and he stands firm [...]. He shall unveil the [...] over them [...], and he draws them to him [...], his will [...], and he [...] them, and he stands them up [...] there, and they remain until [...].
paragraphs.temporal_note: Extended, impersonal description of a resurrection/ingathering operation (“unveil… draws… stands them up”), entirely cosmos→cosmos with no polemical ‘today/nowadays’ anchoring or church application.

Concluding beatitude/exhortation (“Blessed is every one who…”) shifts from descriptive cosmology to reader-facing valuation. Not clearly a Gospel citation, but it functions as a late moralizing/tag ending rather than the schematic core list.
